rationale: X exceeds the references' evidentiary baseline by reproducing the consequential request-level behavior that R1 and R2 leave inferred: failed reloads can clear or partially redraw route sets, the default watcher can consume the change, and correction is picked up on the next request. Its findings agree with the checkout's clear/load/finalize sequence and watcher timing, and the resulting brief covers the requested actors, pain, outcomes, non-goals, acceptance cases, open questions, and further evidence without prescribing implementation. The only notable gaps are that the simultaneous-edit example emphasizes one valid and one invalid file rather than separately stating the both-valid case, and production is scoped out rather than demonstrated as an explicit unchanged counterexample. Those are minor communication/completeness gaps, not material errors, so X is at least at parity overall.

shortcomings.summary: The simultaneous-change acceptance example does not separately spell out the ordinary case where both application and engine edits are valid.
shortcomings.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L49/X.md:73-77 covers an application-valid/engine-invalid interval and recovery after correction, whereas .amp/judge-inputs/L49/R1.md:63-66 and R2.md:65-67 explicitly include both-valid simultaneous changes before the one-invalid variant. X.thread.md:839-874 likewise probes one valid plus one invalid and then both corrected, so the missing wording is narrow rather than an uninvestigated boundary.

shortcomings.summary: Production behavior is only declared a non-goal, not presented as an explicit unchanged acceptance counterexample or re-probed.
shortcomings.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L49/X.md:49-55 excludes production and lines 83-87 define steering evidence, while R1.md:73 and R2.md:23,49-50 make the no-live-reload production counterexample explicit. The scenario is development-focused and asks for non-goals, so this omission does not undermine the requested maintenance brief.

strengths.summary: X directly verifies the central developer-visible failure and recovery sequences instead of presenting source-level inference as fact.
strengths.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L49/X.thread.md:631-645 records a generated development app returning 200 before an invalid save, 500 SyntaxError on the detecting request, and 404 on the unchanged next request; lines 694-745 verify failed initial load, deletion, both reload_classes_only_on_change values, and correction. Lines 766-789, 809-831, and 839-892 extend the same request probes to engine routes, external draw files, simultaneous changes, and deleted files.

strengths.summary: The reported runtime behavior is consistent with the implementation's state and file-watcher semantics.
strengths.evidence: railties/lib/rails/application/routes_reloader.rb:30-40 clears all route sets before loading and restores only the prior loaded state in ensure; activesupport/lib/active_support/file_update_checker.rb:67-107 snapshots the filesystem state before invoking the reload block. railties/lib/rails/application/finisher.rb:192-225 explains why reload_classes_only_on_change=true waits for another detected change while false reruns the reload cycle each request.

strengths.summary: The final deliverable is a comprehensive behavioral brief that keeps the unresolved product choice open and avoids prescribing internals or tests.
strengths.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L49/X.md:9-34 defines actor, pain, and validated current behavior; lines 36-55 define outcomes and non-goals; lines 59-79 cover all requested acceptance boundaries; and lines 83-103 provide steering evidence, open behavioral questions, and evidence still to collect. Lines 40-47 and 89-95 explicitly leave last-good routes versus persistent failure visibility and sibling-route behavior undecided.
